"Authority in terrible battle" and "sovereignty over snake-bites"—thus [are the powers of] the Śmaśānabhoginīs of the intermediate directions. Kuṇḍalā [moves] counter-clockwise from midday through the first, second, third, and fourth watches in the four gates beginning with the left ear; this is the movement of the Śmaśānabhoginīs.
Furthermore, in the external *cakramelāpaka*, there is a movement through the eight gates beginning with the mouth according to the specific times divided into eight watches.
Thus, the movement of the Yoginīs within the external and internal [realms] is twofold:
one is by way of the four faces of Mind, Speech, Wisdom, and Body starting from the East and so forth, following the clockwise rotation of the Kuṇḍalī through the cardinal directions;
the other is by way of the faces of Body, Wisdom, Speech, and Mind, following the counter-clockwise rotation of the Kuṇḍalī through the intermediate directions.

Here, on the eastern petal of the lotus of gnosis, among the spokes of the wheels of mind, speech, and body, and specifically upon the eastern and southeastern spokes and in the eastern and southeastern great cremation grounds (*mahāśmaśāna*), the *Bhoginīs*—by virtue of the nature of the faces of Mind—bestow the accomplishment of rites such as slaying (*māraṇa*).

Likewise, on the southern petal, among the southern and southwestern spokes and in the southern and southwestern great cremation grounds, the *Bhoginīs*—by virtue of the nature of the faces of Speech—bestow the accomplishment of rites such as subjugation (*vaśya*).

Thus, on the western petal, in the western and northwestern spokes, the *Bhoginīs* of the western and northwestern great cremation grounds exist by way of the nature of the Wisdom Face (*jñānavaktra*) and bestow the accomplishment of rites such as paralysis (*stambhana*).

Likewise, on the northern petal, in the northern and northeastern spokes, the *Bhoginīs* of the northern and northeastern great cremation grounds exist by way of the nature of the Body Face (*kāyavaktra*) and bestow the accomplishment of rites such as pacification (*śāntika*).

The mandalas of Vāyu, Agni, Mahendra, and Varuṇa for these [deities]—arisen from the syllables ya, ra, la, and va—are to be understood as their seats in sequence at the heart, throat, navel, and forehead, situated upon their respective spokes.

Thus, according to the division of the four faces of the Blessed One, there is the movement of these [energies] through the movement of the sun and the vital breath (*prāṇa*). By means of that specific time, there is the ritual procedure for worship.
In this way, in all the *Yoginītantras*, there is a movement according to the specific time measured by the *yoginīs*.
In the *Mahāmāyālī*, there is the movement of the four *yoginīs* according to the division of the four junctions (*saṃdhyā*).
Where there are eight yoginīs, they are distinguished by the divisions of the watches (prahara); where there are sixteen, by the divisions of the half-watches;
where there are thirty-two, by the divisions of the ghaṭikās;
and where there are sixty-four, by the divisions of the daṇḍas.
Where there are fifteen, they are so by way of the division of lunar days (tithi);
where there are twelve, they are so by way of the division of zodiacal signs (lagna);
where there are twenty-four, they are so by way of the division of half-zodiacal signs (lagnārdha); and where there are six, they are so by way of the division of seasons (ṛtu).
Where there are three, they exist through the distinction of time;
where there are two, they exist through the distinction of the paths;
where there is one, there is no movement.

In this context, everywhere, the movement of the vital breath (prāṇa) occurs through the differentiation of the channels (nāḍikā); by the various types of movement of the vital breath, there is a distinction of time;
and by that distinction of time, there is the ritual procedure for worship (pūjāvidhi).

In all Yoginītantras, the movement of the female messengers (dūtīs) must be understood everywhere as follows: through the power of that movement, there arise enjoyment, absorption, authority, and sovereignty.
Now, the movement from one station to another for the Kulikā and the female messengers within the gaṇacakra is described.

Here, on the first day of the lunar fortnight, at midnight during the rising of the eastern face, there is a transition (*saṃcāra*) of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, from the central position of the presiding deity (*adhipati*) to the eastern petal;
then, Vajradākinī occupies the position of the Kulikā-presiding deity.
Consequently, by virtue of that position, she who was Vajradākinī becomes the Kulikā.

She who is Vajravārāhī becomes Vajradākinī; therefore, at the morning twilight, with the arising of the southern face, there is the movement of Vajradākinī— the Kulikā— from her position in the center of the presiding deity to the southern petal, while Lāmā moves from the central position of the presiding deity [to the northern petal].
Then, by virtue of the position, she who is the Vajradākinī Kulikā becomes Lāmā, and she who is Lāmā becomes the Kulikā.
Consequently, at the junction of midday, with the rising of the western face, there is the movement of the Lāmā Kulikā from her position in the center of the presiding deity to the western petal.
In the central position of the sovereign of Khaṇḍarohā,
according to the rule of the positions, she who is the Kulikā of Lāmā becomes Khaṇḍarohā, and she who is Khaṇḍarohā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the evening twilight during the rising of the northern face, there is the movement of Khaṇḍarohā the Kulikā on the northern petal,
while Rūpiṇī is in the center in the position of the presiding deity;
thus, by virtue of the position, she who was Khaṇḍarohā the Kulikā becomes Rūpiṇī.
She who is Rūpiṇī becomes the Kulikā;
furthermore, on the following day, the second [day], there is the transition of Rūpiṇī, Kulikā, and the others.
There, at midnight during the dawn, with the rising of the eastern face, there is a transition of Rūpiṇī from her position as the central sovereign to the eastern petal.
In the center, in the place of the sovereign, is the ḍākinī Vajravārāhī; then, by virtue of that position, Rūpiṇī becomes Vajradākinī,
and Vajravārāhī becomes the Kulikā ḍākinī.
Then, at the morning twilight, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, to the southern petal; [there is] Vajradākinī, Lāmā, in the center, the place of the sovereign.
Consequently, by virtue of that position, Vajravārāhī becomes Lāmā.
Lāmā, who is Vajradākinī, becomes the Kulikā;
therefore, at the midday junction, there is the movement of Vajradākinī-Lāmā-Kulikā upon the western petal,
while Khaṇḍarohā-Lāmā resides in the center as the presiding deity.
Then, by virtue of the position, she who is the Vajradākinī Lāmā Kulikā becomes Khaṇḍarohā; she who is Lāmā Khaṇḍarohā becomes the Kulikā.
Thereafter, at the juncture of the afternoon, there is the movement of Lāmā Khaṇḍarohā, the Kulikā, upon the northern petal.
In the center, at the place of the sovereign,
due to the power of that position, she who is Lāmā Khaṇḍarohā Kulikā becomes Rūpiṇī,
and she who was Khaṇḍarohā Rūpiṇī becomes the Kulikā.

Then, on the third day, during the third [watch], there is the movement of Khaṇḍarohā, Kulikā, and the others. There, at the juncture of midnight, with the rising of the eastern face, there is the movement of Khaṇḍarohā, who is the Kulikā in the form of Rūpiṇī, upon the eastern petal;
then Rūpiṇī, who is Vajradākinī, is in the center, in the place of the sovereign.
Consequently, by virtue of that position, she who is Khaṇḍarohā, the Kulikā in the form of Rūpiṇī, becomes Vajradākinī.
She who is Rūpiṇīvajradākinī becomes the Kulikā;
therefore, at the morning twilight during the arising of the southern face, there is the movement of Rūpiṇīvajradākinī-Kulikā upon the southern petal,
while Vajravārāhī-Lāmā resides in the central position as the sovereign.
Then, by virtue of the position, she who is the *rūpiṇī* Vajradākinī Kulikā becomes Lāmā; and she who is Vajravārāhī Lāmā becomes the Kulikā.
Consequently, at the junction of midday, with the rising of the western face, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī—the Lāmā Kulikā—upon the western petal.
In the center, in the position of the sovereign, is Khaṇḍarohā; then, by virtue of that position, Vajravārāhī becomes the lineage-holder (kulikā) Lāmā Khaṇḍarohā,
and [she] becomes the lineage-holder Vajradākinī Khaṇḍarohā.
Then, at the junction of the afternoon twilight, with the rising of the northern face, Vajradākinī Khaṇḍarohā, the Kulikā, arrives at the northern petal;
Lāmā Rūpiṇī is in the center, in the position of the presiding deity.
Consequently, by virtue of that location, she who is Vajradākinī Khaṇḍarohā, the Kulikā, becomes Rūpiṇī.
She who is Lāmārūpiṇī becomes the Kulikā;

therefore, on the fourth day, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Lāmā, Kulikā, and the others. There, at the juncture of midnight, with the rising of the eastern face, the Kulikā in the form of Lāmārūpiṇī moves to the eastern petal.
In the center, in the place of the sovereign, is Khaṇḍarohā-Vajradākinī;

then, by virtue of that position, Lāmārūpiṇī Kulikā becomes Vajradākinī, and [Lāmārūpiṇī] becomes Khaṇḍarohā-Vajradākinī Kulikā. Then, at the morning twilight, with the arising of the southern face, there is the movement of Khaṇḍarohā-Vajradākinī Kulikā onto the southern petal.

Rūpinīlāmā is in the central position of the sovereign; then, by virtue of that position, Khaṇḍarohāvajradākinī is the Kulikā Lāmā. Following that, at the time of the midday junction during the arising of the western face, there is the movement of the Kulikā Rūpinīlāmā upon the western petal.
In the center, in the place of the sovereign, is Vajravārāhī Khaṇḍarohā; then, by virtue of that position, she who is Rūpiṇī, the blue Āmākulikā, becomes Khaṇḍarohā,
and she who is Vajravārāhī-Khaṇḍarohā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the evening twilight of the afternoon, when the north-facing [moon] rises, there is a movement to the northern petal for Vajravārāhī-Khaṇḍarohā-Kulikā;
Vajradākinī-Rūpiṇī is in the central position as the presiding deity; thus, by virtue of their respective positions, Vajravārāhī-Khaṇḍarohā-Kulikā [occupies the north].
She who possesses form is she who has the form of Vajradākinī; she becomes the Kulikā.
Therefore, on the fifth day, on the fifth lunar day, there is the movement of Vajradākinī, Kulikā, and the others.
There, at the juncture of midnight, when the eastern face arises, there is the movement of the Kulikā Vajradākinī-rūpiṇī upon the eastern petal;

Lāmā-Vajradākinī is in the center, in the position of the sovereign. Then, by virtue of that location, she who was Vajradākinī becomes the Kulikā Lāmā-Khaṇḍarohā-rūpiṇī in her own place; and once again, she is Vajradākinī during the first full [moon].
Thereafter, at the eastern twilight, when the southern face arises, there is the movement of the Kulikā Lāmā-Vajradākinī upon the southern petal.

Between Khaṇḍarohā and Lāmā, then, by virtue of their respective positions, she who is Lāmā becomes Vajradākinī Kulikā in the form of Khaṇḍarohā; subsequently, in her own place, she becomes Lāmā again, while she who was Khaṇḍarohā-Lāmā becomes the Kulikā. Then, at the junction of midday, with the rising of the western face, there is the movement of the Kulikā of Khaṇḍarohā-Lāmā upon the western petal.

Then, in the center of Rūpiṇī Khaṇḍarohā, whichever Khaṇḍarohā is present by virtue of her position becomes the Kulikā of the Vajradākinī-Lāmā family of Rūpiṇī; having been so, she returns once again to her own place as Khaṇḍarohā,
while that Rūpiṇī Khaṇḍarohā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the subsequent twilight, with the rising of the northern face, there is the movement of Rūpiṇī Khaṇḍarohā Kulikā to the northern petal;
Vajravārāhī Rūpiṇī remains in the center.
Then, by virtue of the [changing] positions, she who was Rūpiṇī becomes Vajradākinī Lāmā Khaṇḍarohā Kulikā, and once again, in her own place, she becomes Rūpiṇī.

She who has the form of Vajravārāhī, having assumed the forms of Vajradākinī, Lāmā, and Khaṇḍarohā, returns once again to her own place as Kulikā. Thus, on the fifth day, during twenty junctions (*saṃdhyā*), through the transition of the twenty modes of awakening, this movement of Vajravārāhī and the others occurs by way of the division of the lunar dates (*tithi*)—namely Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Riktā, Pūrṇā, the first, second, third, fourth, and fifth—as the nature of the five lunar digits (*kalā*) of the first joy (*ānanda*). Just as it is on the first day, so it is on the sixth;
just as on the second, so on the seventh.
Just as it is on the third day, so it is on the eighth; just as it is on the fourth, so it is on the ninth;
just as it is on the fifth, so it is on the tenth—the transition occurs through non-differentiation from supreme bliss (*paramānanda*).
Thus, as it is on the sixth day, so it is on the eleventh; as it is on the seventh, so it is on the twelfth; as it is on the eighth, so it is on the thirteenth.
As it is on the ninth day, so it is on the fourteenth;
as it is on the tenth, so it is on the full moon. The movement [of the winds] occurs through non-differentiation from the bliss of cessation (*viramānanda*);
at its conclusion, having performed the great piercing (*mahāpīḍa*), there is the movement of the four yoginīs during the first fortnight.
Then, on the first day of the second dark fortnight, from midnight during the first watch, there is the movement of Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground;
Kākāsyā is in the center at the place of the sovereign; thereafter, by virtue of the position, [the movement of] Kulikā [occurs].
Kākāsyā becomes Kākāsyā; she is the Kulikā.
Then, in the second watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyā and Kulikā in the great southern cremation ground, and that of Ulūkāsyā in the center.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā of Ulūkāsyā,
and Ulūkāsyā becomes the Kulikā;
thereafter, in the third watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā, the Kulikā, in the western great cemetery.
Then, in the center of Śvānāsyā, by virtue of their positions, Ulūkāsyā becomes the Kulikā of Śvānāsyā,
and Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is a movement to the northern great cemetery of the dog-faced Kulikā, and to the middle [cemetery] of the sow-faced one; thereafter,
by virtue of the location, the dog-faced Kulikā becomes the sow-faced one.
The sow-faced one (Śūkarāsyā) becomes the lineage-holder (Kulikā);
thus, by means of the clockwise rotation of the right earring, her movement occurs on the solar side according to the division of the four watches.
Then, from midday, on the lunar side during the first watch, the movement of the sow-faced lineage-holder occurs in the great cremation ground of Īśāna.
Then, in the middle of Yamadādhī, according to the requirement of the position, Śūkarāsyā becomes Kulikā Yamadādhī,
and Yamadādhī becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadādhī the Kulikā in the Vāyavya great cremation ground,
and that of Yamadūtī in the center;
thereafter, by virtue of the location, Yamadādhī becomes the Kulikā and Yamadūtī [becomes the presiding deity].
She who is Yamadūtī becomes the Kulikā;
therefore, during the third watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Yamadūtī in the great cremation ground of Nairṛtya,
in the center of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, and she who is Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Kulikā;
thereafter, during the fourth watch, the Yamadaṃṣṭriṇīs move from Kulikā to the great cremation ground of Agni.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Yamadamstrinī becomes Kulikā and Yamamathanī;
that which was Yamamathanī becomes Kulikā.
Thus, by means of the counter-clockwise rotation of Kuṇḍalā, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs in the lunar portion alone;
in this manner, the movement of the Yoginīs on the first day is to be understood.
Furthermore, on the second day, during the first watch from midnight, there is the movement of Yamamathanī Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground.
In the center of Vajravārāhī and Kākāsyā, then by virtue of their respective positions, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā Kākāsyā;
she who is Vajravārāhī-Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, in the second watch, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, in the great southern cremation ground, between Kākāsyā and Ulūkāsyā;
consequently, by virtue of the location, Vajravārāhī, as the Kulikā, becomes Ulūkāsyā.
She who is Kākāsyā and Ulūkāsyā becomes Kulikā;
therefore, during the third watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyā, the Kulikā, in the western great cremation ground,
and that of Ulūkāsyā and Śvānāsyā in the center.
Then, by virtue of the location, the Kākāsyā Kulikā becomes Śvānāsyā;
she who was Ulūkāsyā becomes Śvānāsyā Kulikā.
Thereafter, in the fourth watch, the movement of Ulūkāsyā Kulikā takes place in the northern great cremation ground.
Between the Dog-faced and the Pig-faced [goddesses],
then, by virtue of their positions, the Owl-faced one becomes the Kulikā;
that which is the Pig-faced and the Dog-faced becomes the Kulikā.
Thus is the movement by way of the Kundalī in a clockwise direction on the solar side;
then, on the lunar side, during the first watch from midday, Śvānāsyā and Kulikā move in the great cremation ground of Īśāna,
while Śūkarāsyā and Yamadādhī move in the center.
Then, according to the respective locations, she who is Śvānāsyā becomes Yamadādhī the Kulikā, and she who is Śūkarāsyā becomes Yamadādhī the Kulikā;
thereafter, during the second watch, the movement of Śūkarāsyā Kulikā takes place in the Vāyavya Mahāśmaśāna.
Between Yamadādhī and Yamadūtī,
then by virtue of their positions, Śūkarāsyā becomes Yamadūtī and Kulikā; and she who was Yamadādhī and Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Yamadādhīkulikā in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya; [then] Yamadūtī and Yamadamṣṭriṇī are in the center.
Thereafter, by virtue of the location, Yamadādhīkulikā becomes Yamadamṣṭriṇī.

She who is Yamadūtī is Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī; she becomes Kulikā. Therefore, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamadūtī-Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Āgneya; [she moves] from Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī to Yamamathanī in the center.
Thus, by virtue of the location, Yamadūtī-Kulikā becomes Yamamathanī.
She who is Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī is Mamathānī; she becomes the Kulikā.
Thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of Kuṇḍalā, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs during the lunar portion.
Then, on the third day, again from midnight during the first watch, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī-Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground.
In the center of Yamamathanī and Kākāsyā, then due to the sequence of the positions, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Kākāsyā;
she who was Yamamathanī becomes Kulikā.
Then, in the second watch (prahara), there is the movement of Yamamathanī-Kulikā to the southern great cremation ground.
In the center of Vajravārāhī-Ulūkāsyā, then by virtue of the position, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā-Ulūkāsyā; she who is Vajravārāhī-Ulūkāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, in the third watch, there is the *samāpatti* of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, in the western great cremation ground.
Between Kākāsyā and Śvānāsyā,
by virtue of their positions, Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā of Vajravārāhī;
that which is Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā [of Kākāsyā].
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyā Kulikā in the northern great cremation ground,
and that of Ulūkāsyā and Śūkarāsyā in the center;
thereafter, by virtue of their respective positions, Kākāsyā Kulikā becomes Śūkarāsyā.
She who is Ulūkāsyā (Owl-faced) is Kulikā when she is Śūkarāsyā (Boar-faced);
thus is the movement by way of the right-turning of the earring in the solar portion.

Then, in the lunar portion, during the first watch before midday, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā as Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Īśāna, while Śvānāsyā (Dog-faced), Yamadāḍhī (Fang of Yama), and [Rākṣasī] are in the center.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, Ulūkāsyā becomes Yamadādhī the Kulikā, and she who was Śvānāsyā becomes Yamadadhi the Kulikā;
thereafter, during the second watch, there is the movement of Śvānāsyā, the Kulikā, in the Vāyavya great cremation ground.
Then, in the center, by virtue of their positions, Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā Yamadūtī and Śūkarāsyā becomes the Yamadūtī;
that which was Śūkarāsyā Yamadūtī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of the sow-faced Kuliṅkā in the great cremation ground of Nairṛtya; she is between Yamadamṣṭrī and Yamamathani.
Consequently, by virtue of her position, the sow-faced Kuliṅkā becomes Yamadamṣṭrī.

Yamadādhī, who possesses the fangs of Yama, becomes the Kulikā; thereafter, during the fourth watch, the Kulikā Yamadādhī moves through the great cremation ground of Āgneya. Between Yamadūtī and Yamamathani, by virtue of their respective positions, Yamadādhī becomes Yamamathani, and she who was Yamadūtī-Yamamathani becomes the Kulikā. Thus is the movement by way of the counter-clockwise rotation of the Kundalī.
Then, on the fourth day, during the first watch after midnight, there is the movement of Yamadūtī Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground;
[then] that of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī Kākāsyā in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, Yamadūtī becomes Kākāsyā Kulikā.
She who is Yamadamṣṭriṇī-Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā;
therefore, during the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadamṣṭriṇī-Kulikā in the southern great cremation ground (mahāśmaśāna),
and that of Yamamathanī-Ulūkāsyā in the center.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, Yamadamstrinī becomes Ulūkāsyā Kulikā;
that which is Yamamathanī-Ulūkāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Thereafter, in the third watch, there is the movement of Yamamathanī Kulikā in the western great cremation ground.
In the center of Vajravārāhī Śvānāsyā, then by virtue of the position, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā Śvānāsyā;
she who is Vajravārāhī Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, in the northern great cremation ground;
Kākāsyā and Śūkarāsyā are in the center.
Consequently, due to the influence of the location, Vajravārāhī, as the Kulikā, becomes Śūkarāsyā.
She who has the face of a crow and the face of a sow is the Kulikā;
thus, by the rightward movement of the Kundalī, there is a circulation on the solar side.
Then, on the lunar side, during the first watch from midday, there is the circulation of Kākāsyā Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Īśāna.
Between Ulūkāsyā-Yamadādhyā and [the next], then by virtue of their positions, Kākāsyā becomes Yamadādhī-Kulikā;
she who is Ulūkāsyā-Yamadādhī becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā Kulikā in the Vāyavya great cremation ground,
and of Śvānāsyā Yamadūtī in the center; thereafter, by virtue of their positions, Ulūkāsyā Kulikā becomes Yamadūtī,
and she who was Śvānāsyā Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā.
During the third watch, the movement of the dog-faced Kuliṅkā is in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya,
while that of the sow-faced Yamadamṣṭriṇī is in the center; thereafter, by virtue of their respective positions, the dog-faced Kuliṅkā becomes Yamadamṣṭriṇī.
She who has the face of a boar and tusks that intoxicate is Kulikā;
therefore, during the fourth watch, the movement of Kulikā Śūkarāsyā occurs in the great cremation ground of Āgneya, between Yamadādhī and Yamamathanī.
Then, by virtue of the position, Śūkarāsyā becomes Yamamathanī as Kulikā, and she who was Yamadāḍhī becomes Yamamathanī as Kulikā;

thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the Kundalī, is the movement of the Yoginīs through the lunar mansions. Then, on the fifth day, during the first watch from midnight, there is the movement of Yamadāḍhī, the Kulikā, in the eastern cremation ground.
Then, in the center of Yamadūtī Kākāsyā, by virtue of the [mandala] position, Yamadādhī Kulikā becomes Kākāsyā;
she who was Yamadūtī Kākāsyā becomes Kulikā. Thereafter, in the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadādhī Kulikā in the southern great cremation ground.
Between Yamadamṣṭriṇī and Ulūkāsyā,
then by virtue of their positions, Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā and Ulūkāsyā;
she who is Yamadamṣṭriṇī-Ulūkāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Yamadamṣṭriṇī Kulikā in the western great cremation ground,
and of Yamamathani Śvānāsyā in the center;
thereafter, by virtue of the location, Yamadamṣṭriṇī becomes Śvānāsyā Kulikā.
Yamamathanī, who is Śvānāsyā, becomes the Kulikā; therefore,
during the fourth watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Yamamathanī in the northern great cremation ground,
in the midst of Vajravārāhī, who is Śūkarāsyā.
Then, by virtue of the positions, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā Śūkarāsyā; that Vajravārāhī who is Śūkarāsyā becomes the Kulikā.

Thus, by the clockwise rotation of Kuṇḍalā, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs during the solar portion. Then, during the lunar portion, from midday in the first watch, the movement of the Kulikā Vajravārāhī occurs in the Īśāna great cremation ground, while Kākāsyā, who is Yamadāḍhī, moves in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamadādhī becomes the Kulikā of Vajravārāhī;
she who is Kākāsyā-Yamadādhī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, in the second watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā of Kākāsyā in the great cremation ground of Vāyavya.
Then, in the middle, by virtue of the position, Kākāsyā becomes the Kaulikī Yamadūtī,
while she who is Ulūkāsyā Yamadūtī becomes the Kaulikī.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā Kulikā in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya;
Śvānāsyā is in the center of Yamadamṣṭriṇī; and thereafter, by virtue of their respective positions, Yamadamṣṭriṇī becomes Ulūkāsyā Kulikā.
She who has the face of a dog and fangs of pride is the Kulikā;
therefore, in the fourth watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Śvānāsyā in the great cremation ground of Āgneya, while Sukarāsyā Yamamathanī is in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, she who is Śvānāsyā becomes Yamamathanī the Kulikā, and she who is Śūkarāsyā becomes Yamamathanī the Kulikā;
thus, through the counter-clockwise rotation of the Kundalī, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs within the lunar portion.
Then, on the sixth day, during the first watch from midnight, there is the movement of the sow-faced Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamadādhī, the crow-faced one, is in the center.
Consequently, due to the influence of the location, the sow-faced Kulikā becomes the crow-faced one.

She who is Yamadādhīkākāsyā is the Kulikā (1). Then, in the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadādhīkulikā in the great cremation ground to the south, and that of Yamadūtī-ulūkāsyā in the center;
therefore, by virtue of the location, Yamadādhīkulikā becomes Ulūkāsyā.
Yamadūtī is Ulūkāsyā; she is the Kulikā.
Therefore, in the third watch, the union of Yamadūtī, who is the Kulikā, occurs in the western great cremation ground, in the midst of Yamadamṣṭriṇī and Śvānāsyā.
Then, by virtue of the location, Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā Śvānāsyā;
she who is Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī-Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Thereafter, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī-Kulikā in the northern Great Cremation Ground (Uttaramahāśmaśāna).
Between Yamamathanī and Śūkarāsyā,
then, by virtue of their positions, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes the Kulikā of Śūkarāsyā,
and she who is Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā of Śūkarāsyā.
Thus is the movement by way of the rightward rotation of the *kuṇḍalā* on the solar side;
thereafter, on the lunar side, during the first watch after midday, there is the movement of *Yamamathanī* and *Kulikā* in the great charnel ground of *Īśāna*,
while *Vajravārāhī* and *Yamadādhī* are in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā Yamadādhī;
that Yamadādhī who is Vajravārāhī becomes the Kulikā.
Thereafter, during the second watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Vajravārāhī in the great cremation ground of Vāyavya.
Then, by virtue of the position [in the mandala], Yamadūtī, who belongs to the Vajravārāhī family, becomes Kākāsyā-Yamadūtī;
she who was the Kulikā [Yamadūtī] now becomes Kākāsyā-Yamadūtī.
Consequently, during the third watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyā-Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Nairṛtya.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Kākāsyā becomes Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī in the center of Ulūkāsyā and Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī; that which was Ulūkāsyā-Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Kulikā.
Consequently, in the fourth watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā-Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Agni.
Then, by virtue of the position [of the channels], in the center of Śvānāsyā Yamamathanī, Ulūkāsyā becomes Kulikā Yamamathanī; that which is Śvānāsyā Yamamathanī becomes Kulikā.
Thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the Kundalā, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs in the lunar portion.
Then, on the seventh day, during the first watch from midnight, there is the movement of Śvānāsyā Kulikā in the Great Eastern Cemetery; in the middle [watch], there is Śūkarāsyā and Kākāsyā.
Then, by virtue of the location, Śvānāsyā Kulikā becomes Kākāsyā, and she who was Śūkarāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Then, in the second watch, there is a *samācāra* [ritual gathering] at the southern great cremation ground (*mahāśmaśāna*) of the lineage-holder (*kulikā*) Śūkarāsyā;
in the center [of that] is Yamadāḍhī-Ulūkāsyā.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, the lineage-holder Śūkarāsyā becomes Ulūkāsyā.
Yamadādhī is Ulūkāsyā; she is the Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Yamadādhī-Kulikā in the western great cremation ground, while Yamadūtī is Śvānāsyā in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamadādhī becomes Kulikā Śvānāsyā;
she who was Yamadūtī Śvānāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Thereafter, in the fourth watch, the movement of Yamadūtī Kulikā occurs in the northern great cremation ground.
Between Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī and Śūkarāsyā, then, by virtue of their positions,
Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā and Śūkarāsyā becomes Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī;
thus, through the clockwise rotation of the *kuṇḍalī*, there is the union of the Yoginīs during the solar portion.
Then, during the first watch from midday in the lunar portion, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī Kulikā in the Īśāna great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamamathani is in the center of Yamadādhī;
then, by virtue of the location, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī Kulikā becomes Yamadādhī.
Yamamathanī, who is Yamadādhī, becomes the Kulikā;

therefore, in the second watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Yamamathanī in the Vāyavya Mahāśmaśāna, while Vajravārāhī, as Yamadūtī, is in the center. Consequently, by virtue of the location, the Kulikā Yamamathanī becomes Yamadūtī.

Vajravārāhī Yamadūtī is the Kulikā; therefore, during the third watch, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Nairṛtya, and Kākāsyā Yamadamṣṭriṇī is in the center.
Then, by virtue of the location, Vajravārāhī Kulikā becomes Yamadamṣṭriṇī, and she who was Kākāsyā Yamadamṣṭriṇī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyākulikā in the great cremation ground of Agni,
and that of Ulūkāsyāyamamathanī in the center;
thereafter, by virtue of their respective positions, Kākāsyākulikā becomes Yamamathanī.
She who is the crusher of Ulūkāsyā and Yama is Kulikā; thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of Kuṇḍalā, there is movement within the lunar portion.
Then, on the eighth day, during the first watch after midnight, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā-Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground, and that of Śvānāsyā and Kākāsyā in the middle.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, the owl-faced Kulikā becomes the crow-faced one,
and she who was the dog-faced Kulikā becomes the crow-faced one; thereafter, during the second watch, there is the movement of the dog-faced Kulikā in the great southern cremation ground.

Between Śūkarāsyā and Ulūkāsyā, then by virtue of their positions, Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā of Ulūkāsyā, and she who is Śūkarāsyā becomes the Kulikā of Ulūkāsyā. Then, in the third watch, in the western great cremation ground, there is the *samāpatti* of Śūkarāsyā; between her and Śvānāsyā, then by virtue of their positions, Śūkarāsyā becomes the Kulikā of Śvānāsyā, and she who is Yamadādhīśvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamadādhīkulikā in the northern great cremation ground,
and that of Yamadūtīśūkarāsyā in the center;
thereafter, by virtue of their respective locations, Yamadādhīkulikā becomes Śūkarāsyā.
Yamadūtī, who has the face of a sow, is the Kulikā;

thus, by the clockwise rotation of the Kundalī, there is the movement of the Yoginīs during the solar portion. Then, during the lunar portion, in the first watch after midday, there is the movement of Yamadūtī, the Kulikā, in the great charnel ground of Īśāna.
Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, Yamadādhī, and Yamadūtī; then, by virtue of their positions, Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā,
and Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, Yamadādhī, and she who is [the third] become Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Vāyu;
[the movement] of Yamamathanī and Yamadūtī is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of their respective positions, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Yamadūtī.

Yamamathani is the Yamaduti who becomes the Kulika; therefore, in the third watch, there is a union of the Kulika Yamamathani with Vajravārāhī in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya, in the midst of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, the Kulika Yamamathani becomes Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī.
She who is Vajravārāhī with fangs is the Kulikā;
therefore, in the fourth watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Vajravārāhī in the great cremation ground of Agni, in the center [of the mandala], together with Kākāsyā and Yamamathanī.
Then, by virtue of the [changing] positions, Yamamathani becomes the Kulika of Vajravārāhī; and she who was the Kulika of Kākāsyā-Yamamathani becomes the Kulika [of Vajravārāhī].

Thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the Kundalini, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs during the lunar portion. Then, on the ninth day, in the first watch from midnight, the movement of Kākāsyā-Kulikā takes place in the eastern great cremation ground.
Between Ulūkāsyā and Kākāsyā,
then, by virtue of their respective positions, Kākāsyā becomes Kulikā and so forth, and then again becomes Kākāsyā;
that which was Ulūkāsyā-Kākāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā Kulikā in the southern great cremation ground;
[Śvānāsyā] and Ulūkāsyā are in the center.
Then, by virtue of her own place, having become Ulūkāsyā Kulikā and so forth, she becomes Ulūkāsyā once again.
She who is Śvānāsyā-Ulūkāsyā is the Kulikā;
then, in the third watch, the *samāhāra* of Śvānāsyā-Kulikā occurs in the western great charnel ground, between Śūkarāsyā and Śvānāsyā.

Then, by virtue of her own station, having become the Kulikā and others beginning with Śvānāsyā, she becomes once again Śvānāsyā; she who was Śūkarāsyā becomes Kulikā. Then, in the fourth watch, there is a union (*samāgama*) of Śūkarāsyā-Kulikā in the northern Great Cremation Ground (*mahāśmaśāna*), in the midst of Yamadāḍhī-Śūkarāsyā.
Thereafter, by virtue of her own station, having become the Kulikā and others beginning with Śūkarāsyā, she becomes once again Śūkarāsyā.
She who is Yamadādhī with a boar’s face (*śūkarāsyā*) becomes the Kulikā;
thus, by the clockwise rotation of the earring, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs during the solar portion.
Then, during the lunar portion, in the first watch after midday, there is the movement of Yamadādhī-Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Īśāna.
Then, by the power of her own station, Yamadūtī becomes Yamadādhī in the center; having become Kulikā and the others, she again becomes Yamadādhī.
That which is Yamadūtī and Yamadādhī becomes Kulikā.
Then, in the second *prahara*, there is the movement of Yamadūtī-Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Vāyavya.

Then, by virtue of her own position in the center between Yamadamstrinī and Yamadūtī, Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā and so forth; subsequently, she becomes Yamadūtī again, and that Yamadūtī who was [there] becomes Kulikā.
Yamadamstrinī becomes Yamadūtī, and she who was Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā.

Then, in the third watch, there is the movement of Yamadamṣṭriṇī in the great cremation ground of Nairṛtya belonging to Kulikā; [the movement] of Yamadamṣṭriṇī and Yamamathanī in the center. Then, by virtue of their respective locations, having become Kulikā and the others, Yamadamṣṭriṇī becomes Yamadamṣṭriṇī again, and she who was Yamamathanī becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamamathanī Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Agni;
Vajravārāhī, as Yamamathanī, is in the center. Thereafter, by virtue of her own station, having become Yamamathanī Kulikā and the others, she becomes Yamamathanī once again.
She who is Vajravārāhī becomes Kākāsyā and the others, and then, by virtue of her own place, becomes the Kulikā;
thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of Kuṇḍalā, the movement of the Yoginīs within the lunar portion is to be understood by the Yogin.

Thus, the movement of the Yoginīs through the eight great cremation grounds occurs according to specific times; on the ninth day, the section on movement concludes with their return to their respective places. Then, having performed a grand worship, on the tenth day the movement proceeds as it did on the first day.
On the eleventh day, it is like the second; on the twelfth day, it is like the third;
on the thirteenth day, it is like the fourth.
On the fourteenth day as on the fifth,
on the new moon day as on the sixth, and on the first day of the bright fortnight as on the seventh.

On the second [day], the transition is like that of the eighth; on the third, it is like that of the ninth. Then, by virtue of returning to their respective locations, Vajravārāhī and the others again assume their own individual natures.
Then, having performed the worship again on the fourth day, the movement proceeds as on the tenth; on the fifth as on the eleventh;
on the sixth as on the twelfth; and on the seventh as on the thirteenth.
On the eighth day it is like the fourteenth;
on the ninth day it is like the new moon;
on the tenth day it is like the first day of the bright fortnight.
On the eleventh day, as on the second,

and on the twelfth day, as on the third, there is the movement of the Śmaśānavāsinīs through the divisions of mind, speech, and body; thereafter, by means of nine new days and the conjunction with nine new lunar mansions (nakṣatras), the twenty-seven nakṣatras proceed until the moon reaches the end of the twelve zodiac signs.
Thus, through the fifteen divisions of the moon’s phases (*candrakalā*), there is the movement of the *ḍākinīs* and others together with Heruka;
through the twenty-seven divisions of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), there is the movement of the Crow-faced goddesses (*kākāsyā*) and others.
Then, at the conclusion of the divisions of the moon and sun, the movement of the Fierce Goddesses (*pracandā*) and others occurs for three days.

For example, here on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight, at the rising of the ascendant of Scorpio, having performed worship at the eastern spoke of the *cittacakra*, one should abandon the [central] means (*upāya*) and proceed with the recitation at the southern spoke for Pracaṇḍā; at the western spoke for Caṇḍākṣī; at the northern spoke for Prabhāvatī; and at the eastern spoke for Mahānāsā.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Pracaṇḍā becomes Caṇḍākṣī, Caṇḍākṣī becomes Prabhāvatī, Prabhāvatī becomes Mahānāsā, Mahānāsā becomes Pracaṇḍā, and [the cycle continues].

Then, in the middle of Scorpio, there is the movement of Pūrvapracandā to the western spoke; of Pūrvacandākṣī to the northern spoke; of Pūrvaprabhāvatī to the eastern spoke; and of Pūrvamahānāsā to the southern spoke. Then, by virtue of their positions, Pracaṇḍā becomes Prabhāvatī, Candākṣī becomes Mahānāsā, Mahānāsā becomes Prabhāvatī, Pracaṇḍā becomes Mahānāsā, and Candākṣī becomes Pracaṇḍā.
Thereafter, at the rising of Sagittarius, there is the movement of Pūrvapracandā to the northern spoke.
Pūrvacaṇḍākṣī is on the eastern spoke, Pūrvaprabhāvatī on the southern spoke, and Pūrvamahānāsā on the western spoke.
Then, by virtue of their positions, [the sequence becomes] Pracandā, Mahānāsā, Caṇḍākṣī, Pracaṇḍā, Prabhāvatī, Caṇḍākṣī, Mahānāsā, and Prabhāvatī.
Thereafter, during the half of the lunar month, the movement of Pūrvapracaṇḍā occurs on the eastern spoke.
The movement occurs from Candākṣī at the southern spoke, to Prabhāvatī at the western spoke, and to Mahānāsā at the northern spoke;
thereafter, by virtue of their respective positions, the female messengers (dūtīs) such as Pracandā and the others assume their own forms.

Thus, by means of the clockwise rotation of the earrings, the movement of the four [messengers] in the gaṇacakra must be performed for two and a half *daṇḍas* each during the rising of Scorpio and the half of Scorpio, and during the rising of Sagittarius and the half of Sagittarius.

Then, at the rising of the crocodile (*makara*), having performed worship, there is a movement from the northeast position of Vīramatī to the northwest spoke of Kharvarī, to the southwest spoke of Laṅkeśvarī, to the southeast spoke of Drumacchāyā, and to the northeast spoke of Vīramatī; thus the movement occurs.
Then, by virtue of the positions, she ceases [that movement] and becomes Kharvarī; Kharvarī becomes Laṅkeśvarī; Laṅkeśvarī becomes Drumacchāyā; and Drumacchāyā becomes Vīramatī.

Then, from the Makarārddha, there is a transition of Pūrvavīramatī to the Nairṛtya spoke; of Pūrvakharvarī to the Āgneya spoke; of Pūrvalaṅkeśvarī to the Īśāna spoke; and of Pūrvadrumacchāyā to the Vāyavya spoke.
Consequently, due to the change of position, Pūrvavīramatī becomes Laṅkeśvarī, Pūrvakharvarī becomes Drumacchāyā, Pūrvalaṅkeśvarī becomes Vīramatī, and Pūrvadrumacchāyā becomes Kharvarī.

Then, at the emergence of Kumbha, there is a transition from Pūrvaviramati to the southeast spoke (āgneyāra); from Pūrvakharvarī to the northeast spoke (īśānāra); from Pūrvalaṅkeśvarī to the northwest spoke (vāyavyāra); and from Pūrvadrumacchāyā to the southwest spoke (nairṛtyāra).
Thereafter, by virtue of the positions, Vīramati becomes Drumacchāyā and Kharvarī becomes Vīramati.
Laṅkeśvarī becomes Kharvarī, and Drumacchāyā becomes Laṅkeśvarī; thereafter, there is a movement to the Īśāna spoke by Pūrvavīramatī,
a movement to the Vāyu spoke by Pūrvakharvarī, a movement to the Nairṛti spoke by Pūrvalaṅkeśvarī, and a movement to the Āgneya spoke by Pūrvadrumacchāyā.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, the yoginīs such as Vīramatī and the others assume their own forms;

thus, through the counter-clockwise rotation of Kuṇḍalā, the movement of the yoginīs must be understood by the yogins in the Gaṇacakra within the Cittacakra as follows: during the rising of Capricorn and the first half of Capricorn, and during the rising of Aquarius and the first half of Aquarius, the eight yoginīs move according to the division of the ascendant halves.
Then, having performed the worship, the movement within the speech-wheel (*vākcakra*) should be carried out as follows: here,
at the rising of the sign of Pisces (*mīnalagna*), there is the movement of Airāvatī from the eastern spoke of the speech-wheel to the southern spoke.

In the western spoke of Mahābhairavā is Vāyuvegā; in the northern spoke of Vāyuvegā is Surābhakṣī; and in the eastern spoke of Surābhakṣī is Saṃcarī. Then, by virtue of their positions, Mahābhairavā becomes Airāvatī, Vāyuvegā becomes Mahābhairavā, Surābhakṣī becomes Vāyuvegā, and Airāvatī becomes Surābhakṣī.

Then, in the half-fish [mandala], there is a transition from Pūrvairāvatī to the western spoke; from Pūrvamahābhairavā to the northern spoke; from Pūrva-vāyuvegā to the eastern spoke; and from Pūrva-surābhakṣī to the southern spoke.
Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Airāvatī becomes Vāyuvegā, Mahābhairavā becomes Surābhakṣī, Vāyuvegā becomes Airāvatī, and Surābhakṣī becomes Mahābhairavā.

Then, at the rising of Aries, there is a transference (*saṃcāra*): Pūrvāirāvatī moves to the northern spoke, Pūrvamahābhairavā to the eastern spoke, Pūrvavāyuvegā to the southern spoke, and Pūrvasurābhakṣī moves to the western spoke. Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Airāvatī becomes Surābhakṣī, Mahābhairavā becomes Airāvatī, Vāyuvegā becomes Mahābhairavā, and Surābhakṣī becomes Vāyuvegā.

Then, in the first half of the night, there is the movement of Airāvatī on the eastern spoke, Pūrvamahābhairavā on the southern spoke, Pūrvavāyuvegā on the western spoke, and Pūrvasurābhakṣī on the northern spoke.
Subsequently, by virtue of their respective positions, Airāvatī and the others assume their own specific forms;
thus, through the clockwise rotation of the *kuṇḍalī*, the meeting of the four yoginīs occurs in the speech wheel (*vākcakra*) according to the division of the half-lagna.

Then, having performed the worship at the rising of the bull-lagna (*vṛṣalagnodaya*), the movement of Śyāmādevī occurs from the northeast (*īśāna*) to the northwest (*vāyavya*); that of Subhadrā from the southwest (*nairṛtya*); that of Hayakarṇā from the southeast (*āgneya*); and that of Khagānanā from the northeast (*īśāna*). Consequently, according to their respective positions, Śyāmādevī becomes Subhadrā; Subhadrā becomes Hayakarṇā; Hayakarṇā becomes Khagānanā; and Khagānanā becomes Śyāmādevī.

Then, from the eastern half of the bull, there is the movement of Śyāmādevī to the southwestern spoke; of Subhadrā to the southeastern spoke; of Hayakarṇā to the northeastern spoke; and of Khagānanā to the northwestern spoke.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Śyāmādevī becomes Hayakarṇā, Subhadrā becomes Khagānanā, Hayakarṇā becomes Śyāmādevī, and Khagānanā becomes Subhadrā.

Then, at the rising of the couple, there is a transposition: first, Śyāmādevī moves to the southeast spoke; Subhadrā to the northeast spoke; Hayakarṇā to the northwest spoke; and Khagānanā to the southwest spoke. Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Śyāmādevī becomes Khagānanā, Subhadrā becomes Śyāmādevī, Hayakarṇā becomes Subhadrā, and Khagānanā becomes Hayakarṇā.

Then, in the half-period [of each zodiac sign], there is a movement (*saṃcāra*) of the goddess Śyāmādevī of the east upon the northeast spoke, of Subhadrā of the east upon the northwest spoke, of Hayakarṇā of the east upon the southwest spoke, and of Khagānanā of the east upon the southeast spoke. Then, by virtue of their respective positions, the yoginīs beginning with Śyāmādevī assume their own forms.

Thus, the movement of the four yoginīs is performed by means of the counter-clockwise (*vāmāvarta*) rotation of the *kuṇḍalā*; the movement of the eight yoginīs in the circle of the assembly (*gaṇacakra*) is to be performed according to the division of the half-signs beginning with Pisces (*vāmin*). Then, having performed worship, the movement within the body-circle (*kāyacakra*) is to be performed as follows:

Here, during the rising of Cancer, there is a movement from the eastern spoke of the body wheel (*kāyacakra*) to the southern spoke of Cakravegā, to the western spoke of Khaṇḍarohā, to the northern spoke of Śauṇḍinī, and then to the eastern spoke of Cakravarminī. Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Cakravegā becomes Khaṇḍarohā, Khaṇḍarohā becomes Śauṇḍinī, Śauṇḍinī becomes Cakravarminī, and Cakravarminī becomes Cakravegā. Then, during the latter half of Cancer, there is a movement from the former Cakravegā to the western spoke, from the former Khaṇḍarohā to the northern spoke, from the former Śauṇḍinī to the eastern spoke, and from the former Cakravarminī to the southern spoke.

Then, by virtue of their positions, Pūrvacakravegā becomes Śauṇḍinī; Pūrvakhaṇḍarohā becomes Cakravarminī; Pūrvaśauṇḍinī becomes Cakravegā; and Pūrvacakravarminī becomes Khaṇḍarohā. Subsequently, at the rising of the constellation Siṃha (Leo), there is a transference: Pūrvacakravegā moves to the northern spoke, Pūrvakhaṇḍarohā to the eastern spoke, Pūrvaśauṇḍinī to the southern spoke, and Pūrvacakravarminī to the western spoke.

Then, by virtue of their respective positions, Cakravegā becomes Cakravarminī; Khaṇḍarohā becomes Cakravegā; Śauṇḍinī becomes Khaṇḍarohā; and Cakravarminī becomes Śauṇḍinī. Subsequently, in the eastern half of the lion [mandala], there is the movement of Cakravegā to the eastern spoke, Khaṇḍarohā to the southern spoke, Śauṇḍinī to the western spoke, and Cakravarminī to the northern spoke. Thereafter, by virtue of their own respective positions, the yoginīs beginning with Cakravegā assume their own respective forms.
Thus is the circulation in the body wheel by way of a clockwise rotation starting from Kuṇḍalā;
then, having performed the worship, the circulation must be carried out by way of a counter-clockwise rotation as follows:

In this case, when the Virgo ascendant (kanyā-lagna) arises, Suvīrā moves from the northeast (īśāna) corner to the northwest (vāyavya) corner; Mahābalā moves to the southwest (nairṛtya) corner; Cakravartinī moves to the southeast (āgneya) corner; and Mahāvīryā moves to the northeast (īśāna) corner. Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Suvīrā becomes Mahābalā, Mahābalā becomes Cakravartinī, Cakravartinī becomes Mahāvīryā, and Mahāvīryā becomes Suvīrā.

Then, in the half-square of the maiden (Kanyā), there is the movement of Pūrvasuvīrā to the southwest corner (Nairṛtya), of Pūrvamahābalā to the southeast corner (Āgneya), of Pūrvacakravartinī to the northeast corner (Īśāna), and of Pūrvamahāvīryā to the northwest corner (Vāyavya). Then, by virtue of their positions, Suvīrā becomes the Cakravartinī, and Mahāvīryā becomes Mahābalā.
She becomes a universal sovereign (cakravartinī), very heroic, of great valor, and of great strength;
therefore, at the rising of the sign Libra (tulā-lagna), there is the movement [of the deity] from the eastern Suvīrā to the southeast spoke (āgneyāra).
The movement occurs in the northeast for Pūrvamahābalā, in the northwest for Pūrvacakravartinī,
and in the southwest for Pūrvamahāvīryā.
Thereafter, by virtue of her superior station, she becomes a Suvīrā, possessing great heroism and great strength; as a Suvīrā,
she is a sovereign ruler (cakravartinī) endowed with great power.
Then, Mahāvīryā becomes the Cakravartinī; subsequently, there is the movement from Pūrvasuvīrā to the Īśāna spoke at the end of the scale (tulārdha),
and from Pūrvamahābalā to the Vāyu spoke.
The former Cakravartinī moves from the northwest spoke to the southeast spoke of the former Mahāvīryā;
thereafter, by virtue of their respective positions, the four yoginīs beginning with Suvīrā assume their own individual forms.

Thus, by means of the counter-clockwise rotation of the *kuṇḍalā*, the movement of the yoginīs in the *gaṇacakra* must be performed according to the divisions of the twelve half-lagnas beginning with Virgo (*kanyā*) within the body-wheel (*kāyacakra*). In this way, on the first day, there is the movement of the yoginīs through the twenty-four divisions of the half-lagnas beginning with Scorpio (*vṛścika*). Here, on the thirteenth day, it is according to the division of the mind (*citta*) or the division of the quality of darkness (*tamo-guṇa*).

Likewise, on the fourteenth day— or on the second day— by means of the differentiation of speech or the differentiation of the *rajo-guṇa*, and similarly on the full moon day— or on the third day— by means of the differentiation of body or the differentiation of the *sattva-guṇa*,

the movement of the twenty-four yoginīs must be performed by the yogins in the *gaṇacakra* through the twenty-four divisions of time within the twelve half-signs (*ardhalagna*) beginning with Scorpio.

Thus is the rule for the procedure of the movement of the Yoginīs according to the twenty-four specific times. Here, whichever Yoginī moves from her own station to another place, by virtue of consuming the remains [of offerings] there and by adopting the means (upāya) of that [local] family, she becomes a member of that family until she returns to her own station. Then, by returning to her own station, she becomes established in her own family.
Thus, by means of grasping Heruka and through the power of consuming the remnants of the Kulikā, whichever Yoginī from Ḍākinī up to Yamamathanī enters into the center becomes the Kulikā Vajravārāhī;
and she who is the Kulikā Vajravārāhī becomes a member of that family (*tatkulinī*) through the power of consuming the remnants of others.
In this way, the thirty-six Yoginīs of the families, though previously without family (*akulīnāḥ*), become possessed of family (*kulīnāḥ*).

By virtue of their position, those of noble birth become ignoble, just as according to worldly convention even those of ignoble birth become noble when bathed beneath the jeweled parasol of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*). Just as Viśvāmitra and others, though born from the wombs of dog-cookers and other outcasts and thus of ignoble origin, became Brahmins through the power of mantra, meditation, and austerity; likewise, even noble Brahmins become ignoble by eating beef and the like, or by eating in the houses of outcasts such as Cāṇḍālas.

Likewise, in the *Yoginīsaṃcara*, by means of visiting other locations, partaking of food, consuming [substances], and receiving [initiations], the yoginīs previously mentioned—the thirty-seven beginning with Dombī and so forth—should be recognized by the yogins according to worldly convention (*laukika-saṃvṛti*) for the purpose of moving within the *gaṇacakra*.

Thus, having performed worship, mantra recitation, and meditation for three years, at the conclusion of the mantra recitation, one should perform the fire offering (*homa*). Then, for three fortnights, one should carry out the movement of the yoginīs within the *gaṇacakra*.
Thereafter, all the previously mentioned means for attaining worldly accomplishments (*laukika-siddhi*) as taught in the tantras will always and in every way be accomplished for the practitioner.

Furthermore, by another method, the accomplishment of a single goal is achieved through a single practice— namely, by means of mantra recitation, meditation, and fire-offerings (homa)— yet the yogi does not thereby become accomplished in the primary siddhi. Rather, having accomplished a single practice, such as the siddhi of the sword (khaḍga) or other such siddhis,
this "movement of the Yoginīs" (yoginīsaṃcāra) must be understood by yogis according to specific times, as described in the *Mūlatantra* known as the *Lakṣābhidhāna*.
Alternatively, by means of this commentary,
the rule "therefore it has been said" is for the sake of directly realizing the expansion of all worldly activities and all accomplishments, and for the attainment of the state of a great adept;
such is the procedure for the movement of the Yoginīs.
Now, the seats transformed from the seed-syllables of the locations and names are described both internally and within the external *gaṇacakra*.
Therein, externally, beneath Meru is the mandala of space, transformed from the syllable *haṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the lotus at the crown of the head (*uṣṇīṣa*).
Externally, above that is the mandala of wind, transformed from the syllable *yaṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the lotus at the forehead.
Externally, that [disk] is a fire-mandala transformed from the syllable RAṂ; internally, it is the pericarp of the lotus at the throat.

Externally, above that, is the water mandala transformed from the syllable *vaṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the heart-lotus. Externally, above that, is the earth mandala transformed from the syllable *laṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the navel-lotus. Externally, above that, is Mount Meru transformed from the syllable *maṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the secret lotus. Externally, above that, is the universal lotus (*viśvakamala*) transformed from the syllable *kṣaṃ*; internally, it consists of the eight channels within the vajra-membrane together with the pericarp. Externally, upon the pericarp is the sun mandala; internally, it is the fire of time (*kālāgni*).
Externally, above that, are Umā and Maheśvara; internally, they are the *rajas* and *śukra* located therein.

Externally, above those, is Heruka; internally, he is the innate bliss (*sahajānanda*). When these two have ceased [their movement] through external non-emission, she who arises is Vajravārāhī. She possesses the quality of being indivisible, like the moonlight of the moon which is all-knowing radiance.
Thus, in the sky of the secret place, within the *vajramaṇi*, by means of the phenomena of body, speech, and mind, the innate bliss is called the Blessed Lord Heruka.
Here, Sahajānanda is the fourth, Jñānavajra;
thus the Lord Heruka is four-faced, consisting of the faces of body, speech, mind, and gnosis.
By the very nature of those four faces, the thirty-six Ḍākinīs abide upon the spokes of the wheels in the north, south, east, and west.

Their corpse-seats (*śavāsana*) arise from the transformation of the first letter of their respective locations within the external wheel of knowledge (*jñānacakra*). To the east is a *preta* transformed from the letter Ā; internally, in the navel-lotus, among the sixty channels that carry the mandalas and the four twilight-channels, the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) restrained in the eastern channel and so forth is called the "corpse-seat."

Thus, on the outer [wheel], on the southern spoke is Lāmā, transformed from the syllable *paṃ*; on the western spoke is Khaṇḍarohā, transformed from the syllable *mam*; and on the northern spoke is Rūpiṇī, transformed from the syllable *tam*. Thus it is in the Knowledge Wheel (*jñānacakra*). In the intermediate directions are feces, urine, blood, flesh, and bone. On the outside, in the eight great cremation grounds, in the eastern cremation ground is a corpse-seat transformed from the syllable *śūṃ*, belonging to Kākāsyā; internally, this is the cessation of the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) in the channel of the mouth. Likewise, on the outside, in the south, is one transformed from the syllable *śaṃ*, belonging to Ulūkāsyā; internally, this is the exhaustion of the vital breath (*prāṇakṣaya*) in the channel of the right nostril.

Externally, the transformation of the syllable *pūṃ* is Śvānāsyā on the western spoke; internally, it is the cessation of the apāna wind in the anal channel (*gudanāḍī*). Externally, the transformation of the syllable *klem* is Śūkarāsyā on the northern spoke; internally, it is the cessation of the prāṇa in the left nostril channel (*putanāḍī*). Externally, the transformation of the syllable *bāṃ* is Yamadāḍhī in the northeast, seated upon a corpse; internally, it is the cessation of the prāṇa in the left ear channel.

Externally, in the northwest, the transformation of the syllable *saṃ* is Yamadūtī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the channel of the right ear. Externally, in the southwest, the transformation of the syllable *ghoṃ* is Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the channel of the right eye. Externally, in the southeast, the transformation of the syllable *uṃ* is Yamamathanī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital wind in the channel of the left eye.
Thus, the eight great charnel grounds should be understood as the seats of Kākāsyā and the others in the outer gaṇacakra.
Now, the seats of Pracaṇḍā and the others, which have evolved from the seed-syllables of their respective locations and names, are described.

Here, in the external *cittacakra*, upon the eastern spoke, there is a corpse-seat evolved from the syllable *pūṃ*; this is for Pracaṇḍā. Internally, in the *dharmacakra*, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the eastern channel; according to the definitive meaning (*nītārtha*), and according to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), externally, it is the placement of the syllable *pūṃ* on the head.

Thus, on the outer southern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *jāṃ*, which is Candākṣī; in the inner sense, this refers to the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the right channel (*nāḍī*). According to the definitive meaning (*nītārtha*), this is the placement of the syllable *jāṃ* on the crest-lock (*śikhā*); according to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the same. On the outer western spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *oṃ*, which is Prabhāvatī; in the inner sense, this refers to the cessation of the vital breath in the western channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), the placement of the syllable *oṃ* is above the right ear;

externally, on the northern spoke, it is the transformation of the syllable *aṃ*, which is *savam*; internally, in the great nose, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the northern channel; and at the heart, in the wheel of dharma (*dharmacakra*), according to the interpretable meaning, it is the placement of the syllable *aṃ* on the back of the neck.
Thus is the placement of the seats and seed-syllables (*pīṭhabījanyāsa*).

Likewise, externally in the *cittacakra*, on the eastern spoke, there is the corpse as the seat of Vīramatī, which is the transformation of the syllable *gom*. Internally in the *dharmacakra*, in the eastern channel (*nāḍī*), there is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇanirodha*).
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), this is the placement of the syllable *gom* above the left ear.
Externally, on the wind-spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *rāṃ*, belonging to Kharvarī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the wind-channel.
According to the provisional meaning (*neyārtha*), this is the placement of the syllable *rāṃ* between the eyebrows.
Externally, on the southwest spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *deṃ*, belonging to Laṅkeśvarī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the southwest channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the syllable *deṃ* on the two eyes;

externally, on the southeastern spoke, a corpse transformed from the syllable *māṃ*, and in the shade of the tree; internally, in the southeastern channel, the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) at the wheel of dharma (*dharmacakra*).
According to the interpretable meaning, there is the placement of the syllable *māṃ* at the base of the arms.
Thus is the rule for the seats of the goddesses of the secondary sacred sites (*upapīṭha*) in the mind-wheel (*cittacakra*).

Then, regarding the outer speech-wheel (*vākcakra*), the inner enjoyment-wheel (*sambhogacakra*), and the outer perimeter: thirty-two channels (*nāḍī*) are in the outer perimeter and eight channels are in the inner perimeter; their seats are described here exactly as they are in the dharma-wheel (*dharmacakra*).

On the eastern spoke of the outer speech-wheel, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *kāṃ*, which is the seat of Airāvatī. In the inner perimeter of the inner enjoyment-wheel, on the eastern channel, there is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*).
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the syllable *kāṃ* on the two armpits;

externally, on the southern spoke, a corpse transformed from the syllable *oṃ*, which belongs to Mahābhairavī; internally, on the right channel (*nāḍī*), it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*).
According to the interpretable meaning, there is the placement of the syllable *oṃ* on the pair of breasts.

Externally, on the western spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *triṃ*; internally, this is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the western channel of Vāyuvegā. According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the placement of the threefold action (*triṃkaraṇyāsa*) at the navel. Externally, on the northern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *koṃ*; internally, this is the cessation of the vital breath in the northern channel of Surābhakṣī.
According to the provisional meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the syllable *koṃ* at the tip of the nose;
this is the placement of the seed-syllables for the seats of the goddesses of the fields and sub-fields within the wheel of speech (*vākcakra*).

Thus, externally, on the spoke of Īśāna, the seat is a corpse transformed from the syllable *kaṃ*, which belongs to Śyāmādevī; internally, in the throat-wheel (*kaṇṭhacakra*), it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇanirodha*) in the channel of Īśāna.
According to the provisional meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the *kaṃkara* syllable on the face;

externally, on the northwest spoke, it is the corpse transformed from the syllable *laṃ*, belonging to Subhadrā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the northwest channel (*nāḍī*);
according to the provisional meaning, there is the placement of the *laṃkara* syllable at the throat.

Externally, on the southwestern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *kāṃ*, which is the seat of Hayakarṇā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the southwestern channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), this is the placement of the syllable *kāṃ* at the heart.

Externally, on the southeastern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *hiṃ*, which is the seat of Khagānanā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital wind in the southeastern channel.

According to the *neyārtha* [interpretation], the placement of the seed-syllables for the seats of the *chandohas*, *upachandohas*, and *dākinyas* is as follows: "In the *meḍhra*, there is the *hiṃkāra*-placement. Thus, this is the rule for the seats of the goddesses of the *kṣetras*, *upakṣetras*, *chandohas*, and *upachandohas* within the *sambhogavākcakra* itself. Then, regarding the *kāyacakre*: externally and internally, on the forehead, in the *sahajacakra*, there are sixteen channels (*nāḍīs*) in the outer circle and ten channels in the inner circle; just as they are in the *sambhogacakra*, so too are their seats described here.

Here, on the eastern spoke of the external body-wheel (*kāyacakra*), there is a corpse-seat transformed from the syllable *prem*, which belongs to Cakravegā. Internally, in the inner circle of the innate wheel (*sahajacakra*), it is the cessation of the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) in the eastern channel. According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the placement of the syllable *prem* at the linga. On the southern spoke of the external [wheel], there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *grm*, which belongs to Khaṇḍarohā. Internally, it is the cessation of the vital wind in the southern channel. According to the interpretable meaning, it is the placement of the syllable *grm* at the anus.

Externally, on the western petal, there is the syllable *sauṃ*, transformed from *sauṃ*, which is Saundinī; internally, it is the restraint of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the western channel. According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), this is the placement of the seed-syllable *sauṃ* on the pair of thighs. Externally, on the northern petal, there is the syllable *suṃ*, transformed from *suṃ*, which is Cakravartinī; internally, it is the restraint of the vital breath in the northern channel. According to the interpretable meaning, this is the placement of the seed-syllable *suṃ* on the pair of shanks. Thus is the placement of the seed-syllables for the seats of the *melāpaka*, *upamelāpaka*, and *dūtī* goddesses within the body wheel (*kāyacakra*).

Then, here on the outside, on the northeast spoke (*īśānāra*), there is the seat (*āsana*) consisting of a *savam* transformed from the syllable *nam*, which belongs to Suvīrā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇanirodha*) in the *niśāna* channel.
According to the definitive meaning (*nitārtha*), this is the placement of the *nam* syllable on the toes; according to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the same.

On the outside, on the northwest spoke (*vāyavyāra*), there is the seat consisting of a *savam* transformed from the syllable *sim*, which belongs to Mahābalā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the *vāyavya* channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the syllable *Siṃ* on the two heels;

externally, on the spoke in the southwest, there is the self-nature (*svabhāva*) resulting from the transformation of the syllable *Maṃ*, which belongs to Cakravartinī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) in the southwestern channel (*nāḍī*).

According to the interpretable meaning, there is the placement of the syllable *Maṃ* on the two big toes; externally, on the spoke in the southeast, there is the self-nature resulting from the transformation of the syllable *Kuṃ*, which is the seat (*āsana*) belonging to Mahāvīryā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the southeastern channel.

According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the seed-syllable *kum* on the two knees; this is the placement of the seed-syllables for the seats of the deities of the cremation grounds (*śmaśāna*) and the secondary cremation grounds (*upaśmaśāna*) within the body wheel (*kāyacakra*).

Thus is the rule for the seats of the residents of the meeting places (*melāpaka*), the non-meeting places (*upamelāpaka*), and the cremation grounds and secondary cremation grounds within the body wheel.

Just as externally there are vehicles for the *preta*s and *ḍākinīs* for the purpose of traveling to the *pīṭhas* and other sites, so too internally there is the movement of the vital winds (*prāṇavāyu*) through all the elements. Just as externally the vital winds abide in their respective channels (*nāḍī*) of the wheels (*cakra*), so too, for the sake of the definitive meaning (*nītārtha*), they abide in their respective channels of the wheels by means of the yoga of breath-retention (*kumbhaka*). Here, in the external *gaṇacakra*, after consecrating the seats of the thirty-six female messengers (*dūtī*) seven times with the previously mentioned seed-syllables—purified by means of human skin and corpses—their respective seats should be assigned to their own locations. Such is the rule for the seating of the Lord and the Wisdom Consort. In this *gaṇacakra*, the generation of *Pracaṇḍā* and the others, as well as the *ḍākinīs* and the rest, occurs from their own name-initial seed-syllables. Having consecrated them with those very same seed-syllables, one must perform the transition from one location to another. This is the rule in all tantras.
Now, the *samayaguḍikā* (vow-pill) for the purpose of purifying the mouth and other parts is described.
When there is an eclipse of both the moon and the sun within a single month—
first that of the moon and subsequently that of the sun— or when in that same month it is first the sun and subsequently the moon, [the pill is to be taken] in that month.

In this context, during a lunar eclipse at the time of the entry of the first lunar day (*pratipad*), one should worship a twelve-year-old or sixteen-year-old fair-complexioned maiden who has not yet given birth with all necessary offerings. Taking her as the support for the deity, one should insert the *vajra* into the lotus and, with the utterance of *hūṃ phaṭ*, emit the *bodhicitta*.

Having emitted it, one should place a lotus-vessel below and, having drawn it up with the *vajra*, pour it into that lotus-vessel. On the second day, having performed worship to the deceased, the marrow should be extracted.
On the third day, having performed worship of a non-Aryan cow, Ratnasambhava should be taken from a menstruating woman;
on the fourth day, one's own vajra-water should be taken;
on the fifth day, the vidyā should be taken.

Thus, one *māṣaka* of semen (*śukra*), two *māṣakas* of marrow (*majjā*), three *māṣakas* of Ratnasambhava, four *māṣakas* of vajra-water (*vajrodaka*), and five *māṣakas* of Vairocana; in this way, through the differentiation of the increase of qualities by one, two, three, four, and five, the five substances are to be taken over the course of five days for space, wind, fire, water, and earth.

Then, having performed the worship of the corpse on the sixth day, human flesh should be taken; on the seventh, horse-flesh; on the eighth, elephant-flesh; on the ninth, dog-flesh; and on the tenth, beef—one *ekākṣa* measure, two *akṣa* measures, three *akṣa* measures, four *akṣa* measures, and five *akṣa* measures respectively. Having taken these as lamps and combined them with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*), [one should prepare] seventy-five *māṣaka* [weights].

Then, on the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight while still fasting, one should drink as desired—either honey-wine (*mādhvīka*), cow’s milk wine (*gauḍī*), grape wine (*drākṣā*), wine from palm trees and the like, or wine made from grain or flour—and together with fifteen *amṛtamakṣikā* flies, one should vomit it up.

With that vomited substance held in a skull-cup, one should grind those ten substances totaling seventy-five *māṣakas*. Then, having taken a jackal’s gallbladder, one should place [the powder] inside it.

Then, having joined the two skull-cups as a vessel, at that very time of night in a cremation ground, one should dig a single cubit deep in a triangular shape upon the ground where a woman who entered the fire together with a corpse has been burned. Having worshipped there with perfumes, incense, and so forth, and having offered a most magnificent *bali* offering, [one should recite] this mantra-ritual:
OM VAJRAKRODHEŚVARĪ SARVADRAVYĀṆI VIŚODHAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ. This is the mantra for purifying the *bali*.
May the Buddhas, the fathers together with their mothers, along with their sons, servants, and circles of kinsmen, come here,
surrounded in their entirety by hosts of divine deities, bringing satisfaction to the sublime Vajrasattva.
32 Thus is the invocation of all the Tathāgatas.
33 Oṃ Śrī Heruka ākattaya ākattaya praveśaya praveśaya bandhaya bandhaya toṣaya toṣaya. 34 Enter, enter! Bind, bind! Satisfy, satisfy!
35. *Sarvadākinīnāṃ hṛdayam* (The Heart of all Dākinīs): *Jah hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ hūṃ phaṭ*. This is the mantra for summoning the *ḍākinīs*.
37 OṂ SUMBHA NIḤSUMBHA HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ | OṂ GṚHṆA 38 GṚHṆA HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ | OṂ GṚHṆĀPAYA GṚHṆĀPAYA 39 HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ | OṂ ĀNAYA HO BHAGAVĀN VAJRAVIDYĀ-
40 RAJA HUM HŪM PHAṬ | This is the mantra for the offering of the bali.
41. Then, having offered the water for honor (*argha*), the water for the feet (*pādya*), and so forth: OM ŚRĪVAJRA HE HE RU RU KAM 42 HUM HŪM PHAṬ DĀKINĪJĀLASAMVARAM SVĀHĀ.
Having empowered [the materials] one hundred and eight times with this mantra, one should cast them into that pit. 43.
One should fill the pit at the head with funeral ashes and offer a great lion [seat].
With this mantra, "OM VAJRAVAIROCANĪYE SVĀHĀ," one should perform the protection.
Having performed [the rite], he should return to his own home and recite the Caturvaktra-mantra during the four junctions (saṃdhyā) on the twelfth day;
the eight-line mantra on the thirteenth day; and the twenty-four-line mantra on the fourteenth day.
Then, on the new moon day or during a solar eclipse, having extracted [the substance] with human fat...
One should prepare pills the size of fifty *mudga* beans.
By means of that pill, food, drink, and so forth, when sprinkled with [the water] produced from the *kuṇḍagolaka*, become purified.
When placed in the mouth, purification of the mouth occurs.
In the gaṇacakra, even at the time of meditation, all protection is secured. Thus is the rule for the procedure of the pill (gulikā).
57 58 59 Now, in the great wheel of the assembly (*mahāgaṇacakra*), regarding those previously mentioned, such as the *dombī*s and the *śūdra*s:
The procedure for the consumption of food and drink by the thirty-six family messengers (kuladūtī) is now described.

61. Here, in this secluded house, in a well-concealed place, all the family messengers (*kuladūtī*) are naked; 62. and the twenty-four practitioners (*sādhaka*), adorned with the five seals (*pañcamudrā*), are in their respective places with their hair loose, as are the yoginīs; 63. the practitioners have their hair tied in topknots.
64. Seated upon human skins; the Lord of the Gaṇas [is seated] in the center of the wheel upon a cow or tiger skin.
65. Then, having made a mat (pattalikā) of human skin one cubit in size, he should give it to the Leader of the Gaṇa, and a mat of horse skin to the Yoginīs of the east.
One should give a strip of dog skin to the yoginīs of the south, a strip of elephant skin to the yoginīs of the west,
a strip of cow skin to the yoginīs of the north,
a strip of buffalo skin to the yoginīs of the northeast, and a strip of donkey skin to the yoginīs of the northwest.

Having given a strip of jackal skin to the Yoginīs of the southwest and a strip of camel skin to the Yoginīs of the southeast, he should then give to the Yoginīs for drinking a skull of one of his own kinsmen who have died— whether it be in one piece,
two pieces, or three pieces— as it may be obtained.

72. Then, having placed the food in a leaf-plate and the drink in a lotus-bowl, the practitioner should circumambulate [the deity] three times, worship with perfumes, flowers, incense, and so forth, 73. and make a formal request. 74. Then, he should dedicate [the merit].
"By this merit, may all sentient beings become attainers of the knowledge of Mahāmudrā.
This *gaṇacakra* should be performed by the king,
either through the power of common mantras or by the constraint of the deities.
Otherwise, there will be a flaw for the practitioners. The common *gaṇacakra* should be performed according to the customs of one's country and family,
with noble women who have been nurtured in their own homes for the sake of accumulating merit.
Otherwise, the gaṇacakra does not exist without the bliss of wisdom and means.
79. That which is devoid of the tasting of sexual union and the bodhicitta, consisting merely of food and drink, is called *vīrabhojya* (the hero’s feast), not a *gaṇacakra*.
80. That very [feast] must be performed with the preceptor at its head.

With eighty-one lay practitioners (upāsakas), the teacher (ācārya) in the Mantra system is also of three kinds: householder, novice (cellaka), and monk; these are the inferior, middling, and superior [levels]. Thus it is said.
Even if a householder has fully understood the ten principles, he is not equal to one who has been consecrated and authorized,
because of the words spoken by the Blessed One in the Tantra regarding the distinction between those two—
the householder and the renunciant.
