85. At the time of exposition, even though they have been honored by the guru, the monks who uphold the vows must perform a salutation while placing the True Dharma and so forth at the forefront; not at any other time when there is no exposition.
87. At any other time, one must show all forms of respect toward a guest who has arrived, such as by offering a seat and so forth.

88. Having abandoned improper acts of veneration (asatkarma-vandanā); 89. having abandoned such things as washing the feet [with improper substances], and having abandoned veneration through body, speech, and mind, one should perform reverence toward wealth and other [offerings].

90. Regarding the ninety cubits [distance] between the householder and the *cellaka* (monastic attendant), it is by the monks. 91. Furthermore, regarding the monk who was previously [ordained], again, regarding the monk who was previously [ordained]:
there is a rule that the monks must perform prostrations at all times to the Guru who has been consecrated as a Vajrācārya and made a Vajradhara.
91. Regarding householders and cell-attendants;
Even though they have not attained [the status of] Arhats, monks and even the lord of men should perform prostrations to them.
Therefore,
there is no confusion among the consecrated householders, cellakas, and monks,
by virtue of their characteristics as senior and junior.
95. Here, between two householders, the one consecrated first is the elder;
96. likewise, between two novices (cellakas), and similarly between two monks (bhikṣus), the one consecrated first [is the elder].
97. The eldest [becomes so] by virtue of his prior position;

97. just as the son of a universal monarch (cakravartin), when consecrated, becomes a universal monarch; a prince, when consecrated, becomes a king; and the son of a minister, when consecrated, [becomes a minister]. 98. [Thus it is.]

99. "The monk becomes the [highest] master (ācārya), the initiate (cellaka) becomes the middle master, and the householder becomes the lowest master. Therefore, among these three, first the monk and afterwards the Vajradhara is made the leader of the assembly (gaṇanāyaka) in the gaṇacakra, the consecration, and other rites; in his absence, the initiate; and in his absence as well, the householder."

99. When a monk who is an *ācārya* is not made the leader (*gaṇanāyaka*) by the donor, even though he is available, then through this transgression of honoring those worthy of honor, there occurs a reversal of merit for the donors due to the defilement of the saffron-colored mark (*kāṣāyaliṅga*). 99. Thus, one endowed with all virtues, who bears the banner of the Omniscient One and has abandoned the ten unwholesome paths of action, should be made the leader.

One who is merciless, wrathful, cruel, stubborn, greedy, unrestrained, self-exalting, a householder who eats from a small dish, a servant, a plowman, a merchant, a seller of the True Dharma, or a fool— such a person should not be made a leader of the assembly by a donor seeking the bliss of Buddhahood. Thus, the Vajrācārya, who bears the banner of the Omniscient One, should be positioned facing east by the patron at the *vīrabhojya* feast.

On its right side, a row of monks and Vajradhara Ācāryas, from the eldest to the youngest, should be arranged facing east. Then, according to the order of eldest to youngest, a row of novice (cellaka) Ācāryas should be arranged facing north, starting from the southwest (nairṛtya) up to the southeast (agni).
A row of householder (gṛhastha) Ācāryas should be arranged facing south, starting from the northeast (īśāna) up to the northwest (vāyu), according to the order of eldest to youngest.
Having placed the leader of the assembly (gaṇādhipati) at the beginning, a row of monk Ācāryas should be arranged starting from the northwest (vāyavya) up to the southwest (nairṛtya).
First, food, drink, and so forth should be prepared.

In the absence of a dust mandala in the center, a square should be made with cow-dung water; having performed worship there with perfumes, flowers, and so on, one should place a single *karmamudrā* on the left side of the Lord of the Gaṇas after forming the *mudrā* of the Lord of the Gaṇas. Otherwise, drinking by the Lord of the Gaṇas without a *yoginī* is not prescribed, even in the context of the *vīrabhojya*.

Therefore, the donor must certainly present a seal to the leader of the assembly for the sake of increasing merit. However, in a case where between a monk and a Vajradhara the elder is ignorant and the junior is the instructor, the junior is the leader of the assembly;
the elder, being ignorant, should be gratified in another house.

99. Likewise, in another tantra, even though they have been consecrated, yoginīs are to be worshipped separately in a house during the *vīrabhojya* feast; first, the nuns who have been consecrated face east according to their seniority (*jyeṣṭha*) or juniority (*kaniṣṭha*); the female novices (*cellikā*) who have been consecrated face north; the laywomen (*upāsikā*) who have been consecrated face south; and the masters (*ācārya*) should be placed by the patron (*dānapati*) on the left of the leader (*gaṇanāyikā*).

Otherwise, meat-eating is not prescribed for the Lord of the Gaṇa (*gaṇādhipati*) in the *vīrabhojya* (hero’s feast) without a specific method; therefore, the donor must certainly present a method to the Lord of the Gaṇa.

The remainder of the mandala and so forth is as before. In the center, food and drink and so forth are first [offered]; thereafter, the various kinds of solid and soft foods should be distributed by moving counter-clockwise from the left of the Lord of the Gaṇa and the others.
The drink should be served in shallow bowls (*śarāva*) or in vessels such as coconut shells.

Then, having purified, awakened, ignited, and transformed into nectar the liquor and other offerings, and having presented the bali offering and so forth, one should sprinkle them with the previously mentioned pill. Then,
one should purify with the left hand using the syllable *Oṃ*, awaken with the right hand using the syllable *Āḥ*,
and ignite by covering them with cupped hands using the syllable *Hūṃ*.

Having rendered [the substance] into nectar with the *garuḍamudrā* and the syllable *hoṃ*, one should draw a triangle, the *dharmodaya*, on the ground with a drop of wine using the ring finger of the left hand.

In its center, one should draw a circle, a drop (*bindu*), and in the middle of that, the wheel of gnosis (*jñānacakra*) consisting of thirty-seven deities, which is transparent and like a magical reflection (*pratisenā*). One should perform its libation according to the procedure to be described:

by means of the letters of the names of the field protectors (*kṣetrapāla*) and so forth, together with the name of the city or village; the name is joined with the first and last letters, or it consists of two letters, the first and the last.
A name consisting of three syllables may be formed using odd-numbered syllables from the beginning, middle, or end [of the name].
For example: *OM* at the beginning, the name in the middle, and *AH HŪM* at the end: *OM amuka AH HŪM BALI GRHṆA GRHṆA SARVASATTVĀṆĀM ŚĀNTACITTAṂ KURU KURU SVĀHĀ*.
Likewise, having consecrated with the mantra "OM HĀRĪTIPIṆDAKE KṢĪM PRATICCHA SVĀHĀ" for Hārītī’s piṇḍaka,
and "OM DŪTIKE AGRAGRĀSAṂ PRATĪCCHA SVĀHĀ OM ĀM HŪM" for the two piṇḍakas of the messenger (Dūtī), one should place them on the ground until the end of the meal.
OM KHAKHA KHĀHI KHĀHI UCCHIṢṬABALIṂ UCCHIṢṬABHAKṢAKA SVĀHĀ. This is the mantra for the *ucchiṣṭabali*. At the appropriate time, everything should be performed individually;
thereafter, the food and drink should be consumed by all the preceptors together with their disciples.
When someone engages in dispute or quarrel, he should be expelled;
however, if a novice or a householder displays pride, one should then inquire about his capabilities.
If he demonstrates capabilities such as the five supernormal knowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) and so forth, then he shall be the leader (*gaṇanāyaka*) over all in all matters.
Otherwise, due to pride in [mere] scriptural learning or pride in having received initiation, a novice or a householder does not become a leader of the gaṇa;
rather, he who was previously a monk is the leader of the gaṇa everywhere.

Now, if one who has been excluded from the *vīrabhojya* (hero’s feast) requests a share, then a penalty regarding food, drink, and so forth must be given to him by the lord of the gaṇa. This rule is to be applied everywhere by the patron (*dānapati*) in the circle of the gaṇa and at the *vīrabhojya*.
Now the procedure for the accomplishment of the mantra is described.

The verses to be spoken here are taught for the purpose of drawing the mandala and for the accomplishment of the mudrās and mantras, as follows: "In mountain caves and thickets, on the shores of the great ocean, and in the cremation grounds where primordial siddhis reside—there one should draw the mandala."
Thus, the Blessed One has taught the specification of locations for the purpose of accomplishing worldly attainments through the expansion of ritual activities.
Having drawn the mandala to be described there in the aforementioned location, one should accomplish immobilization, delusion, and pinning on a mountain;
having drawn the mandala in a ravine or a place thick with trees, one should accomplish subjugation and summoning.

Having drawn a maṇḍala on a grove or on the shore of a clear lake, one should accomplish peaceful and nourishing rites. Having drawn a maṇḍala on the shore of a great ocean, one should accomplish rites of hatred, eradication, and killing.

Having drawn a maṇḍala in a cremation ground, the mantra practitioner should accomplish the extraction of the Ḍākinī-mantra, which is the "primordial accomplishment" (*ādisiddhi*); likewise, he may accomplish worldly accomplishments (*laukikasiddhi*).
Here at the edge [of the cremation ground], one should accomplish the accomplishment of hidden treasure (*nidhānasiddhi*).
One should accomplish the attainment of jewels in a thicket;

one should accomplish the attainment of the elixir in a bower; one should accomplish the attainment of the sword on the shore of the great ocean; one should accomplish the attainment of the ointment in a cremation ground.
Furthermore, one should accomplish [the goal] here by means of the mantra according to the procedure taught in the Tantra.

First of all, having drawn a great maṇḍala in a cremation ground and performed worship, on the full moon day of Caitra in the first year, one should offer the *argha* for the root mantra and recite the root mantra using a rosary of human teeth. One should recite it three hundred thousand times every month. On each full moon day beginning with the fifth [of the lunar fortnight], one should perform a fire sacrifice (*homa*) consisting of a tenth part [of the recitation] using the substances mentioned in the *Karmaprasara*.

In this manner, one should recite the mantra thirty-six hundred thousand times over the course of one year, and perform thirty-six thousand oblations (*homa*) with the root mantra: *oṃ śrīvajra he he ru ru kaṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ ḍākinījālasaṃvara svāhā*. Then, in the second year, according to that same procedure, one should recite the heart-mantra for one year and perform oblations.
"OM HRĀM HRĪM HREM HŪM PHAṬ"— this is the six-syllable heart mantra;
by that same procedure, in the third year, one should recite the subsidiary heart mantra and perform fire offerings.
OM HRĪḤ HAHA HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ—this is the seven-syllable subsidiary heart mantra (*upahṛdayamantra*).
Then, by that same procedure, one should recite and perform fire oblations (*homa*) with the armor mantra (*kavacamantra*) in the fourth year:
OM HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ HIṂ HAṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Thus ends the eight-syllable armor mantra (*kavaca-mantra*).
Then, in the fifth year, by that same procedure, one should recite and offer oblations (*homa*) with the heart mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*) of Vajravārāhī:
OṂ VAJRAVAIROCANĪYE SVĀHĀ.
Thus, having [recited] the ten-syllable heart mantra through the purification of the ten perfections (*daśapāramitā*),
he should then, in the sixtieth year, recite the mantra of the Goddess’s armor (*devīkavaca*) according to that same procedure and perform fire offerings (*homayet*):
OM VAṂ YOṂ MOṂ HRĪṂ HREṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Thus is the eight-syllable Great Armor Mantra (*mahākavacamantra*).

In this way, for the six mantras, a recitation (*japa*) of twenty-one million, one hundred and sixty thousand should be performed over six years; then a fire offering (*homa*) of twenty-one lakh and sixty thousand must be made. At that time, purification of the body occurs for the practitioners of yoga.
Now, for the sake of purifying the four faces, the recitation of the mantra of the four faces is described.

Here, at the time of the transit of the sun into Capricorn (*makara-saṃkrānti*), having drawn the maṇḍala upon the shore of the great ocean and having offered the *argha* oblation to the Ḍākinī, one should perform three hundred thousand recitations (*jāpa*) every month, with a fire sacrifice (*homa*) consisting of one-tenth that number. On each full moon day, [one should recite] the mantra of the eastern face together with the names of the Vajraḍākinīs, ending in *hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*:
OṂ SUMBHA NIḤSUMBHA VAJRAḌĀKINĪ HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Thus is the mantra of the eastern face consisting of fourteen syllables.

One should recite it nine hundred thousand times over three months and perform nine thousand fire offerings (*homa*) with the rosary mentioned in the *Karmaprasara-sādhana*—using human bone beads for the first month, camel bone beads for the second, and donkey bone beads for the third—and one should perform the fire offerings with the substances mentioned in the *Karmaprasara*. Then, at the transition of the sun into Aries (*meṣa-saṃkrānti*), having drawn a mandala in a cave and offered the water-offering (*argha*) to Lāmā, one should recite the mantra of the southern face three hundred thousand times each month and perform the fire offering with a tenth part of that amount during each full moon.

In the first month, with a rosary of lotus seeds; in the second, with a rosary of red sandalwood seeds; in the third, with a rosary of red guñjā seeds—thus, nine hundred thousand recitations and nine thousand fire offerings (homa) should be performed with the mantra:
*OM GRHŅA GRHŅA VAJRALĀME HŪM HŪM PHAṬ*.
Thus, one should recite the twelve-syllable mantra of the right face nine hundred thousand times and perform nine ten-thousand oblations (*homa*).

Then, at the transit of the sun into Cancer, having drawn a mandala on a mountain and offered the water of honor (*argha*) to Khaṇḍarohā, one should recite the mantra of the western face three hundred thousand times each month and perform oblations with a tenth part of that amount.

In the first month, one should recite [the mantra] with a rosary of *putrajīva* seeds; in the second, with a rosary of *rudrākṣa* seeds; and in the third, with a rosary of *riṣṭikā* seeds. The practitioner of mantra (*mantrī*) should perform the fire-oblation (*homa*) with the substances prescribed in the *Karmaprasara*. The mantra is: OM GRHṆĀPAYA GRHṆĀPAYA VAJRAKHAṆDAROHE HUM HŪM PHAṬ.

Thus, one should recite the mantra of the western face, which consists of eighteen syllables, nine hundred thousand times and perform nine ten-thousand oblations (*homayet*). Then, at the transit of the sun into Libra (*tulā-saṃkrāntau*), having drawn a mandala in a bower and offered the water of respect (*argha*) to Rūpiṇī, one should recite the mantra of the northern face three hundred thousand times each month and perform thirty thousand oblations with the substances prescribed for the expansion of ritual activities (*karmaprasara*).
In the first month, [the recitation is performed] with a rosary of crystal beads; in the second, with a rosary of pearl beads; in the third, with a rosary of conch-shell beads.
In this manner, over the course of three months, one should recite nine hundred thousand times and perform ninety thousand oblations.

"OM ĀNAYA HO BHAGAVAN VAJRAVAJRARŪPINI HŪM HŪM PHAṬ"—one should recite this eighteen-syllable mantra of the northern face and perform fire offerings (*homa*). Thus, in one year, one should recite thirty-six hundred thousand times and perform three hundred thousand fire offerings with sixty thousand oblations;
thereafter, the purification of the faces occurs.
Now, the recitation of the mantra for the sake of purifying the mouth, ears, and so forth is described.

Here, in the second year, at the transit of the sun into Capricorn (*makara-saṃkrānti*), having drawn a mandala upon the great ocean and having offered the *argha* oblation to Kākāsyā, one should perform the recitation for fifteen days during the first fortnight using a rosary of human teeth, reciting fifteen *ayuta*s (150,000) of the eight-line [mantra]. During the second fortnight, one should use a rosary of camel teeth, and during the third, a rosary of donkey teeth.
Thus, in one and a half months, one should recite four hundred and fifty thousand (*sārdha-catur-lakṣa*) and perform four hundred and fifty thousand (*sārdha-catur-ayuta*) fire offerings (*homa*).
Thus, with the substances mentioned in the *Pūrvavaktrakarmaprasara*:
"Oṃ namo bhagavate vīreśāya vajrakākāsye huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
This nineteen-syllable mantra is for the first foot.

Then, having drawn a mandala in a hollow at the base of a water-jar and having offered the *argha* oblation to Ulūkāsyā, one should perform the recitation of the mantra four hundred thousand times using the rosary mentioned for Lāmā, together with a fire sacrifice (*homa*) consisting of one-tenth that amount.
*Oṃ mahākalpāgnisaṃnibhāya vajrolūkāsye huṃ hūṃ phaṭ*—
this is the eighteen-syllable mantra of the second line.

Then, at the transit of the sun into Capricorn, having drawn the maṇḍala on the mountain and offered the *argha* to Śvānāsyā, one should recite four hundred thousand [mantras] and a half over the course of one and a half months according to the sequence prescribed for the Khaṇḍarohā rosary, and perform the fire-oblation (*homa*) with a tenth part of that amount.
Oṃ jaṭāmakutoṭkaṭāya vajraśvānāsye huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
This is the seventeen-syllable mantra of the third line.

Then, at midday on a Monday, having drawn a mandala in a grove and having offered the *argha* to Śūkarāsyā, one should recite [the mantra] four hundred thousand times together with Rūpiṇī according to the procedure for the rosary, and perform forty-two thousand *homa* offerings.
*Oṃ daṃṣṭrākarālograbhīṣaṇamukhāya vajrasūkarāsye huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.* This is the twenty-two-syllable mantra of the fourth line.

Then, at the Karkatoḍaya lotus pond, having drawn a maṇḍala like a forest grove and offered the *argha* to Yamadādhi, one should recite [the mantra] for four and a half lakṣas along with half a month according to the procedure for the rosary as taught by Rūpiṇī; one should perform the fire oblation (*homa*) with a tenth part of that amount.
*Oṃ sahasrabhujabhāsurāya vajrayamadādhi huṃ hūṃ phaṭ*.
This nineteen-syllable mantra is the fifth-pada mantra.

Then, on Mount Siṃhārdhadina, having drawn the maṇḍala and offered the *argha* to Yamadūtī, one should recite [the mantra] for three fortnights—four hundred thousand and a half times—according to the procedure for the rosary taught by Khaṇḍaroha. Having performed the fire sacrifice (*homa*) with a tenth part of that number, one should dismiss [the deity].
"Oṃ, to the bearer of the axe, the noose, the raised trident, and the khaṭvāṅga; O Vajra-Yamadūtī, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
This is the mantra of the sixth quarter consisting of twenty-five syllables.

Then, at the transit of the sun into Libra (*tulā-saṃkrānti*), having drawn a maṇḍala in a garden and offered the *argha* to Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, one should recite [the mantra] for four hundred and fifty thousand times along with a period of one and a half months, according to the sequence of the rosary beads mentioned by Lāmā, and perform forty-five thousand fire offerings (*homa*).
Oṃ vyāgrājināṃbaradharaya vajradaṃṣṭriṇi huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
This is the twenty-syllable mantra of the seventh step.

Then, at midday on the day of the scorpion (the twentieth lunar day), having drawn a mandala on the shore of the ocean—or in the absence of the ocean, having drawn a mandala on the bank of a salt-water pond—one should offer the *argha* with the Yamamathanī mantra and recite the mantra for three fortnights according to the procedure for the rosary taught by Vajradākinī, totaling four hundred and fifty thousand (*lakṣa*) repetitions. On each full moon day, one should perform fire offerings (*homa*) until they reach four hundred and fifty thousand (*ayuta*).
The twenty-second syllable mantra of the eighth section is: *OM MAHĀDHŪMĀNDHAKĀRAVAPUṢĀYA VAJRAYAMAMATHANI HŪM HŪM PHAṬ*.
In this manner, one should recite [the mantra] thirty-six lakhs in one year and perform thirty-six ayutas of fire offerings (homa).
Thereupon, purification of the channels of the mouth, anus, nose, ears, and eyes occurs.

Now, the recitation of the mantra for each of the twenty-four limbs is described. Here, if a seashore is not available, one should prepare a mandala on the bank of a salt-water pond. On the new moon day of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, having offered the *argha* with the *Pracaṇḍā* [mantra], one should perform fifty thousand recitations over five lunar days and perform five thousand fire offerings (*homa*).

Thus, having performed one hundred and fifty thousand mantra recitations and fifteen thousand fire offerings over fifteen days, one should perform fifty thousand mantra recitations using a single rosary string as prescribed for Vajradākinī.
OM KARA KARA VAJRA-PRACANDE VAJRAKANDAKAPĀLIN HUM HŪM PHAT. This twenty-syllable mantra is the first mantra for the limbs (pratyaṅga).

Then, on the full moon day of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, having drawn a maṇḍala in a cave, a garden, or a forest, one should recite the *argha* mantra of Candākṣī and perform eleven thousand five hundred fire offerings (*homa*).
OM KURU KURU VAJRACANDĀKṢI VAJRAMAHĀKĀKĀLA HŪM HŪM PHAṬ. This is the twenty-syllable mantra of the second line.

Then, on the new moon day of the month of Pauṣa, having prepared a maṇḍala on a mountain and having offered the *argha* to Prabhāvatī, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and fifty thousand times using the rosaries prescribed for Khaṇḍarohā over the course of fifteen lunar days, and perform ten thousand five hundred fire offerings (*homa*).

OM BANDHA BANDHA VAJRAPRABHĀVATI VAJRAKAKĀLAS HUM HŪM PHAT. This nineteen-syllable mantra is for the third step. Then, on the full moon of the month of Pauṣa, having drawn a maṇḍala in a bower or on the bank of a lotus pond, and having offered an *argha* oblation to Mahānasā, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and fifty thousand times over fifteen days using rosaries made of beads from the *rūpinī* plant, and perform ten thousand five hundred fire offerings (*homāḥ*). OM TRASAYA TRĀSAYA VAJRAMAHANĀSE VAJRA VIKATADAṂṢṬRIN HUM HŪM PHAT.
Thus is the twenty-three-syllable mantra of the fourth line.

Then, on the new moon day of the month of Māgha, having drawn a maṇḍala in a bower or on the bank of a lotus pond, and having offered the *argha* oblation to Vīramatī, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and fifty thousand times using the rosaries mentioned for Rūpiṇī over the course of a fortnight, and perform one hundred and fifty thousand burnt offerings (*homayet*).
